body.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal M_N\) and \(\theta\in[-1,1]\), the semiparametric variance bound for \(\mu_Y-\theta\mu_D\) in the exact labeled experiment \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{coll}}(P)\), with its source-specific propensities \(e_s(x)\), is exactly \(V_{\mathrm{coll}}(P,\theta)\). Consequently, at \(\theta=\theta_T\) the local information for the ratio coordinate is \(\mu_D^2/V_{\mathrm{coll}}(P,\theta_T)=T_{\mathrm{coll}}(P)\). If \(\{x:p_T(x)>0\}\not\subseteq\mathcal H_s\) for every \(s\), no score measurable with respect to any single source block can represent the pathwise derivative of \(\mu_Y-\theta\mu_D\) while retaining the observed supports: every feasible representer must have nonzero components in at least two source blocks. Thus a collection-only-support law is outside every support-retaining single-source fixed-geometry experiment, rather than an algebraic reparameterization of one.
body.justification: This identifies the collection program with the exact pooled observed-data information and gives a formal non-subsumption criterion for collection-only support.
body.gap: Dahabreh et al. identify transported means under union support, and Su et al. optimize regular multi-source weights, but neither derives the source-specific-propensity information bound for a null residual or proves failure of every support-retaining single-source representation.
body.consumer: A trial repository can decide whether its evidence geometry is genuinely collection-only before applying a single-source weak-IV analysis.
